finding: A version IS exportProject() and nothing more: restoring a version reverts pages, styles, settings and metadata, and leaves CMS records, media assets, saved components and templates exactly as they are — four separate stores the snapshot never saw.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:657 `const project = this.composer.exportProject()` inside captureSnapshotAsync; Composer.ts:604-614 returns {version,pages,styles,assets:[],metadata,settings} — no collections, no components, no media. The siblings live in their own IndexedDB databases: ComponentStorage.ts:15 `aquibra-components`, CollectionStorage.ts:13 `aquibra-cms`, media/IndexedDBAdapter.ts:44, versions in VersionHistoryStorage.ts:19 `aquibra-versions`.
fix: Either widen the snapshot (add collections/components/asset manifests to ProjectData and have each manager contribute at capture) or state the boundary on screen: board 163:167's confirm currently reads 'Your current work is saved first — nothing is lost', which is only true of the four things the snapshot carries. Say what a restore does NOT touch.

finding: A restored version can reference data that no longer exists: pages restored from a snapshot still carry asset ids, collection ids and component ids, and those stores were never rolled back — so an element bound to a deleted collection field or a deleted media asset comes back pointing at nothing.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:307 `this.composer.importProject(deepClone(version.snapshot))` is the ONLY write a restore performs; Composer.ts:542-598 importProject touches elements, styles, settings and metadata and nothing else. CollectionStorage/ComponentStorage/media adapters are never consulted.
fix: On restore, diff the snapshot's referenced ids against the live stores and report the dangling set before importing — the same pre-flight shape `runPrePublishChecks` already uses on the publish side.
chain: Versions -> NamedVersion.snapshot -> restoreVersion -> importProject -> CMS / Media / Components -> dangling ids silently survive the restore, with no listener reconciling them

finding: Undo covers exactly what exportProject covers. Anything living outside ProjectData produces an EMPTY patch and is dropped, so Undo stays armed and points at an earlier, unrelated edit — the failure mode the code's own comment names.
evidence: HistoryManager.ts:377-379 `captureSnapshot(){ return deepClone(this.composer.exportProject()); }`; :200-204 `const patch = createPatch(previousState,newState); if (isPatchEmpty(patch)) return;`. Only two features declare themselves out-of-history: BaseBindingManager.ts:106,125,134 and MediaCommandLayer.ts:108 — four call sites of noteUnrecordedAction for the whole editor.
fix: Audit every manager that mutates persistent state outside ProjectData (CollectionManager, ComponentManager, MediaManager, templateSync) and make each call `history.noteUnrecordedAction(<user-facing label>)` on write, the way the CMS binding path already does — or give them real inverse commands.

finding: Brand tokens have two homes and undo only reaches one: the project copy (settings.designTokens) is on the undo stack and in every version, while the registry's localStorage copy is neither — so an undone or restored brand comes back on the next reload.
evidence: DesignSystemTab.tsx:540-547 writes BOTH `composer.setProjectSettings({...designTokens})` and `persistAll()`; TokenRegistryContext.tsx:197-224 `localStorage.setItem(storageKey, JSON.stringify(versioned))`. Only the first reaches exportProject (Composer.ts:613 `settings: this.projectSettings`).
fix: Make the localStorage copy a cache seeded FROM projectSettings rather than a peer source, or re-run persistAll from the SETTINGS_CHANGE handler so the two never disagree.

finding: Undoing the FIRST brand apply cannot visually revert it: the applier bails when the restored token list is empty, so every CSS custom property the apply set stays on the document root.
evidence: ProjectTokensApplier.tsx:36 `if (!incoming?.length) return;` — the effect only ever calls `document.documentElement.style.setProperty` (:50) and never removeProperty. Undo/version-restore reach it via SETTINGS_CHANGE / PROJECT_LOADED (:55-56).
fix: Track the properties this applier has set and removeProperty the ones absent from the incoming list before returning, so an empty token list is an instruction rather than a no-op.

finding: Secrets that the project store deliberately redacts are written in plaintext into every version snapshot, into the unsaved-work record, and into the payload mirrored to the server.
evidence: StorageAdapter.ts:180-193 strips `settings.integrations.email.apiKey` and `settings.publishing.publishedPassword` before every browser write (:206 localStorage, :227 sessionStorage, :286 IndexedDB). The other three writers take the raw export: VersionHistoryStorage.ts:71 `store.put(storedVersion)`, unsavedRecovery.ts:40 `localStorage.setItem(..., JSON.stringify({project,...}))`, versionSync.ts:60 `payload: version as unknown as Record<string,unknown>`. Version export writes them to a downloaded file too (VersionHistoryStorage.ts:322-334).
fix: Move `redactSecretsForBrowserStorage` off StorageAdapter and onto the boundary every writer shares — either `exportProject()` itself with an opt-in `{includeSecrets:true}` for the real save, or a shared `redactForAtRest()` in shared/utils that all four writers call.

finding: exportProject drops two fields ProjectData declares: `pagesOrder` and `dsSchemaVersion`. Every snapshot, every undo checkpoint and every autosave therefore omits the DS migration version, so the migration runner re-decides from whatever the server row happens to carry.
evidence: Composer.ts:604-614 returns six keys; ProjectData declares pagesOrder at project.ts:36 and dsSchemaVersion at :50. BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:295 re-derives pagesOrder from sorted pages on read and :327 reads dsSchemaVersion off the site row, not off the project payload; useComposerInit.ts:193 `const fromVersion = data.dsSchemaVersion ?? 0`.
fix: Emit both fields from exportProject, or delete them from ProjectData — a declared field no writer sets is a claim the type makes and the code does not keep.

finding: PAGE_RECOVERED has no listener. RecoveryManager recreates a missing page root as an EMPTY container and announces it to nobody — and the very next autosave persists that empty page over the real one.
evidence: RecoveryManager.ts:180-197 builds `{children: []}` and emits `EVENTS.PAGE_RECOVERED, {page}`; grep for EVENTS.PAGE_RECOVERED across src/ returns exactly that one emit and zero `.on(` sites. Autosave is armed on PROJECT_CHANGED with only a dirty check (StorageAdapter.ts:47-56; useComposerInit.ts:525-551).
fix: The shell should listen, suspend autosave, and show a blocking notice naming the page — 'This page's contents could not be found; saving now would replace it with an empty page.' The Pages panel should mark the page, and the History panel should offer the newest version that still has it.
chain: Recovery -> PageData.root -> ensurePageRootExists recreates an empty root -> PAGE_RECOVERED -> (nothing listens) -> autosave writes the empty page to the server and the user's page contents are gone with no warning

finding: RUNTIME_FAULT_CAUGHT has no listener. Every uncaught error and unhandled rejection in the editor is announced on the bus and nothing reacts — no autosave pause, no snapshot, no report.
evidence: RecoveryManager.ts:101 `this.composer.emit(EVENTS.RUNTIME_FAULT_CAUGHT, {source, reason})`; zero `.on(EVENTS.RUNTIME_FAULT_CAUGHT` anywhere in src/. The only downstream consumer is a side channel — the sessionStorage sentinel at :95, read by RecoveryBanner.tsx:55.
fix: Listen in the shell: pause autosave, call `keepUnsaved(siteId, composer.exportProject())` so the work survives the reload the user is about to do, and forward `reason` to Sentry with the editor's state. The banner then has something real to offer.
chain: Recovery -> CrashRecord -> handleRuntimeFault -> RUNTIME_FAULT_CAUGHT -> (nothing listens) -> the tab keeps autosaving through a broken state and the crash sentinel is the only trace, so the next load claims 'Recovered your work' over work nobody kept

finding: STORAGE_ERROR is emitted when the local autosave fails and has no listener anywhere. A browser autosave that throws — quota, private mode, disabled storage — is completely silent.
evidence: StorageAdapter.ts:48-52 `this.save(...).catch(error => this.composer.emit(EVENTS.STORAGE_ERROR, {error, operation:'auto-save'}))`; that is the ONLY named use of EVENTS.STORAGE_ERROR in src/ — no subscriber. Its three sibling events are worse: STORAGE_SAVED, STORAGE_LOADED (events.ts:442-443) are declared and named nowhere at all.
fix: Subscribe in the shell and route it into the same save-state machine `useSaveCallback` already owns, so the topbar chip can say 'Not saved on this device' instead of continuing to read Saved.
chain: Storage -> ProjectData -> autoSave -> STORAGE_ERROR -> (nothing listens) -> Topbar keeps reading 'Saved' while nothing has been written locally

finding: VERSION_EXPORTED and VERSION_IMPORTED have no listeners. Exporting or importing a version file — a bulk operation over the user's entire history — completes with no confirmation, no count, and no error path.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:367-371 and :385-389 emit both with a count; grep returns those two emits and zero subscribers. Compare VERSION_PRUNED, whose listener at VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:156 renders the notice at :387-394.
fix: Toast both from the shell using the payload's `count`/`filename` the events already carry, and give importVersions a failure branch — `JSON.parse(text)` at VersionTimelineManager.ts:380 is unguarded, so a wrong file throws into whatever called it.
chain: Versions -> VersionHistoryExport -> exportVersions / importVersions -> VERSION_EXPORTED / VERSION_IMPORTED -> (nothing listens) -> a 50-version import lands or fails with the panel saying nothing either way

finding: The undo stack silently discards its oldest entries at 100 and the event for saying so is declared and never emitted, so a long editing session loses its early history with no notice at the moment it becomes irreversible.
evidence: HistoryManager.ts:613-630 `trimHistory(){ while(this.undoStack.length > this.config.maxHistory) this.undoStack.shift() ... }`, maxHistory = THRESHOLDS.HISTORY_MAX_SIZE = 100 (config.ts:108). EVENTS.HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING exists at events.ts:133 and is named nowhere in src/.
fix: Emit HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING from trimHistory when it first shifts, and have the History panel suggest a named version — the one thing that survives the trim. This is also the honest trigger for the milestone suggestion `useAutoMilestone` already renders.
chain: History -> HistoryEntry -> trimHistory -> HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING (never emitted) -> Versions / MilestoneSuggestionBanner -> the user is never told to save a milestone before the oldest hundred edits become unreachable

finding: An undo or redo that fails because the recorded patch no longer matches the tree bails with a console.warn and NO event, so a broken Cmd+Z is indistinguishable from a dead key. HISTORY_NOOP only covers the empty-stack case.
evidence: HistoryManager.ts:495-499 (`catch(err){ this.undoStack.push(current); console.warn(...); return false; }`) and :584-588 for redo — neither emits. HISTORY_NOOP is emitted only at :469 and :564, both behind `!this.canUndo()` / `!this.canRedo()`. useHistoryFeedback.ts:175-189 is the only handler and can therefore never speak for the bail.
fix: Emit HISTORY_NOOP with a distinct reason ('this step can no longer be applied') from both catch blocks; useHistoryFeedback already renders `data.reason` verbatim at :182.
chain: History -> HistoryEntry.patch -> undo / redo -> (no event on the diverged-patch bail) -> useHistoryFeedback -> Cmd+Z does nothing and says nothing, three keystrokes in a row

finding: restoreEntry returns false on failure and every one of its three callers discards the return, so a failed time-travel restore closes the drawer and changes nothing, with no message.
evidence: HistoryManager.ts:707-742 returns false at :710, :715 and in the catch at :739-741. Callers: HistoryTab.tsx:197 `composer?.history?.restoreEntry(entryId); setShowScrubber(false);` — return dropped, drawer closed unconditionally; ActivityView.tsx:369, :375 and :384 likewise.
fix: Have restoreEntry emit a failure event (or have callers branch on the boolean) and keep the drawer open on failure — closing it is the strongest signal the product gives that something worked.
chain: History -> HistoryEntry -> restoreEntry -> false -> (return discarded at HistoryTab.tsx:197) -> Time-Travel drawer closes as if it succeeded and the canvas is unchanged

finding: The two restore paths make opposite safety guarantees. The Saves-list restore takes a safety version first and aborts if it cannot; the history restore takes none, creates no version, clears the redo stack and truncates the undo stack — and it is the one behind the unconfirmed doors.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:289-299 creates 'Before restoring "<name>"' and returns false if that save throws. HistoryManager.ts:707-742 has no equivalent: :721 `this.redoStack = []`, :724 `this.undoStack = this.undoStack.slice(0, entry.index + 1)`. Confirmed unfixed this session.
fix: Route restoreEntry through the same safety snapshot — call `composer.versions.createVersion('Before jumping back to <label>')` before restoreSnapshot, and abort on failure exactly as VersionTimelineManager does. The confirm boards (W-H-01, W-H-17) are the other half; this is the engine half.
chain: History -> HistoryEntry -> restoreEntry -> (no VERSION_CREATED, no safety snapshot) -> Versions -> everything after the scrub point is unrecoverable, while the sibling restore promises on screen that nothing is lost

finding: History entry ids are stack INDICES, and the stack mutates underneath the rendered list — so a click on a history row can restore a different point than the one it names. This is a wrong restore, not a failed one, and it is unconfirmed and irreversible.
evidence: HistoryFormatter.ts:29 `id: \`undo-${i}\``. HistoryManager.ts:615 `this.undoStack.shift()` renumbers every remaining entry once the stack passes 100 (config.ts:108); :156-160 empties and re-seeds the stack on PROJECT_LOADED. restoreEntry then resolves the stale id against the CURRENT stack (:708-710) and finds a different entry at that index.
fix: Give every HistoryEntry a generated stable id at record time and key the display entries on it, so a stale id resolves to nothing instead of to the wrong step. Until then, restoreEntry should verify the entry's `timestamp` matches the caller's before importing.
chain: History -> HistoryDisplayEntry.id (= stack index) -> trimHistory / PROJECT_LOADED reset -> restoreEntry -> Canvas -> the editor jumps to a point the user did not pick and the steps between are truncated

finding: The Saves panel reports a successful restore whether or not one happened: the hook throws away the manager's boolean, so 'no exception' is read as success — including the path where the safety save failed and the restore was deliberately abandoned.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.restoreVersion returns false at :278 (version not found) and :298 (safety save failed). useVersionHistory.ts:100-106 declares `restoreVersion: (id) => Promise<void>` and `await composer.versions.restoreVersion(id)` — the boolean is dropped. VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:206-208 `await restoreVersion(versionId); if (target) pushToast(\`Restored to ${formatTime(target.createdAt)}\`, 'success')`.
fix: Return the boolean through the hook and branch on it: false must produce the failure toast, not the success one. The abandoned-restore case deserves its own copy — the work was NOT replaced, which is the good news.

finding: VERSION_LOAD_FAILED does two unrelated jobs, so a failed safety save during a restore swaps the panel to the list-read error screen and tells the user 'Only this list failed to load' — which is false: the list is fine and the restore is what stopped.
evidence: Emitted for the storage read at VersionTimelineManager.ts:120 and for the failed safety save at :297. useVersionHistory.ts:57-60 sets `loadError` on either. VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:292-307 then returns the whole load-error screen with the copy 'Your versions are still stored. Only this list failed to load.'
fix: Split the event — VERSION_RESTORE_FAILED for :297 — and render it as an inline failure on the restore confirm band, not as a whole-panel error state.

finding: The unsaved-work safety net only covers network failures. A save refused for auth expiry, changed role, or any generic server error keeps nothing — and the reload then seeds 'Saved · just now' over the gap, which is exactly the incident the module was written to prevent.
evidence: keepUnsaved has two call sites and both are inside `if (isNetwork)`: useSaveCallback.ts:178 and useComposerInit.ts:590. The branches that return without it: PROJECT_NOT_LOADED (useSaveCallback.ts:214-235), isForbiddenSaveError (:239-247), isAuthSaveError (:249+), and the generic tail. useComposerInit.ts:229 `const unsaved = readUnsaved(siteId)` — when it is null, :252 sets `{status:'idle', lastSavedAt: Date.now()}`.
fix: Call keepUnsaved for every failure mode where the edit exists only in the tab — i.e. every `siteId` failure that is not SaveConflictError. The docblock at unsavedRecovery.ts:1-16 already argues the general case; the wiring stopped at the one failure that was measured.

finding: Keeping the unsaved snapshot is best-effort and its failure is invisible. A project larger than the localStorage budget keeps nothing, and the reload then reports 'Saved · just now' — the same false green the record exists to prevent, and it fails hardest on the biggest sites.
evidence: unsavedRecovery.ts:38-45 `try { localStorage.setItem(keyFor(siteId), JSON.stringify({project, at})) } catch { /* quota or storage disabled */ }` — the catch is empty and keepUnsaved returns void, so no caller can know. Nothing writes a fallback and nothing checks the size first.
fix: Make keepUnsaved return a boolean, and when it is false raise a persistent 'Your work could not be kept for the next reload — do not close this tab' notice. Consider IndexedDB (the version store already handles multi-MB payloads) instead of localStorage for the record.

finding: The recovery record carries no idea of what the server had, and never expires — so 'Restore my edits' can silently overwrite a newer server copy, including one a teammate saved, with a full-project import.
evidence: UnsavedWork is `{project: ProjectData; at: string}` — unsavedRecovery.ts:29-33; there is no version, no server updatedAt, no site revision. useComposerInit.ts:246-250 `onClick: () => { instance.importProject(unsaved.project); setIsDirty(true); ... clearUnsaved(siteId) }` — a whole-project replace with no comparison. The toast copy (:236-241) says 'The version on screen is the server's' and never says restoring discards it.
fix: Stamp the server's updatedAt into UnsavedWork at keep time, compare it on read, and when the server has moved on, offer the conflict dialog BuildrikSyncProvider already owns rather than a bare Restore. Expire records older than a session.

finding: The recovery banner announces 'Recovered your work · N pages' when nothing was recovered. It fires on the crash sentinel alone, and in the shipping editor the load path is a server fetch — so any uncaught error or unhandled rejection produces a confident claim about work that was never kept.
evidence: RecoveryBanner.tsx:55 `RecoveryManager.consumeLastCrash()` is the ONLY input; :74 renders 'Recovered your work · <relTime> · N pages. It was kept on this device'. `pageCount` comes from the live composer (AquibraStudio.tsx:478), not from anything recovered. The sentinel is set by any window `error` or `unhandledrejection` (RecoveryManager.ts:64-78, 92-99). The unified-editor load is `loadProject(siteId)` from the dashboard (useComposerInit.ts:186), which reads no local draft.
fix: Gate the banner on a recovery that actually happened — `readUnsaved(siteId) !== null`, or a flag set by whatever restored something — and when only the sentinel is present say what is known: the editor hit an error last session, here is the retry.

finding: The banner's 'Discard & reload' deletes a localStorage key nothing writes, so it discards nothing and is a plain reload — while sitting beside 'Keep changes' as if the two were opposites.
evidence: RecoveryBanner.tsx:34 `const LOCAL_DRAFT_KEY = 'buildrick-project'` and :64 `localStorage.removeItem(LOCAL_DRAFT_KEY)`. The live writer is StorageAdapter.ts:32-35, `keyPrefix: 'aquibra'` → `this.storageKey = 'aquibra-project'`. `buildrick-project` is only ever produced by the one-shot legacy rename at storageMigration.ts:16, guarded by MIGRATION_FLAG_V1 (:63-65).
fix: Point both the banner and the fallback reader at the key StorageAdapter actually writes, or move the key into STORAGE_KEYS and have StorageAdapter read it from there — this is a two-writer, three-reader disagreement over one string.

finding: In the no-siteId editor the local-draft fallback cannot restore anything: it reads the wrong key AND expects a wrapper shape the writer never produces, so a previously autosaved project falls through to 'create a default page'.
evidence: useComposerInit.ts:359-368 reads `localStorage.getItem('buildrick-project')` then requires `saved.project` or `saved.content`. StorageAdapter.ts:206 writes the bare ProjectData (`JSON.stringify(this.redactSecretsForBrowserStorage(data))`) under `aquibra-project` (:32,35) — no wrapper, different key. Neither branch matches, `loadedFromStorage` stays false, and :380 creates a fresh default page.
fix: Read the same key StorageAdapter writes and accept the bare ProjectData shape (`saved.pages`), keeping the two legacy shapes as fallbacks.

finding: The storage-keys SSOT file states a rule the live code breaks: it says legacy `aquibra-` keys exist only as migration sources, while the project autosave still writes one on every tick.
evidence: storageKeys.ts:5-7 'Legacy `aquibra-` prefixed keys exist only in storageMigration.ts as the "old key" side of the migration map.' StorageAdapter.ts:32 `keyPrefix: 'aquibra'`, :35 `this.storageKey = ${this.config.keyPrefix}-project`, written at :206.
fix: Either move StorageAdapter onto STORAGE_KEYS.CURRENT_PROJECT or correct the comment — an SSOT doc that is wrong about its own scope is worse than none.

finding: Every version's visual snapshot is null, always: the capture looks up an element id that exists nowhere in the codebase. The Time-Travel scrubber's entire preview mechanism is built on that field, so it can never show a frame.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:993 `document.getElementById('editor-canvas')` then `if (!canvas) return null` (:994). A repo-wide grep for 'editor-canvas' returns three READERS (VersionTimelineManager.ts:993, TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:162, ActivityView.tsx:46/373) and zero writers — no id="editor-canvas" anywhere. TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:111-112 `findNearestSnapshot(...)` → `setPreviewSrc(nearest?.visualSnapshot ?? null)`; findNearestSnapshot itself skips every version at :54 `if (!v.visualSnapshot) continue`.
fix: The canvas mounts engine HTML in a div, not a <canvas>, so toDataURL was never the right mechanism either. Either set the id and capture with html2canvas-style rasterisation, or delete visualSnapshot and give the scrubber a real preview (a lightweight re-render of the reconstructed snapshot) — the current code is a preview feature with no picture behind it.

finding: There is no time-based checkpointing at all: auto-checkpoints fire on one event, `template:applied`, and the interval config that would provide the rest is declared, defaulted and read by nothing. A user who never clicks '+ Save a version' and never applies a template has an empty version history.
evidence: versions.ts:88 `autoCheckpointEvents: ['template:applied']`; VersionTimelineManager.ts:141-149 subscribes to exactly that list. `autoCheckpointInterval` appears twice in the repo — its declaration (versions.ts:70) and its default (:82) — and in no consumer.
fix: Decide the retention story out loud. If the founder call at versions.ts:83-87 stands (no checkpoint on open), the honest replacement is a checkpoint on a real edit boundary — the HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING of MOD-G-12, or an idle-time interval that finally uses autoCheckpointInterval. Delete the field if neither is wanted.

finding: The prune notice promises a protection that does not exist: it tells the user 'the approved one was kept', and nothing in the version model or the prune knows what approval is.
evidence: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:391 'Past {pruned.kept}. Named versions and the approved one were kept.' pruneVersions protects only `isAutoCheckpoint === false` (VersionHistoryStorage.ts:236-238 `versions.filter(v => v.isAutoCheckpoint).slice(-excess)`). NamedVersion (versions.ts:19-42) has no approval field; approval is fetched from the server's review status (SavesChrome.tsx:76-83) with no version id on it — SavesChrome's own docblock says so: 'reviews.status carries state, reviewer and time, not a version number'.
fix: Drop the clause, or give the approval a version id on the server so the prune can honour it. As written it is a data-safety promise nothing keeps.

finding: An auto-checkpoint that fails to write becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which the recovery manager catches as a crash — so a full version store makes the next reload claim 'Recovered your work'.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:142-146 `const handler = () => { if (!this.isLoading) { this.autoCheckpoint(...) } }` — not awaited, no catch. saveVersion rethrows on any non-quota error and on a second quota failure (VersionHistoryStorage.ts:94-104); when every stored version is named, `pruneVersions` returns 0 at :240-242 and the retried `writeVersion` throws again. RecoveryManager.ts:70-77 turns that rejection into the crash sentinel, which RecoveryBanner.tsx:55 reads.
fix: Catch inside the handler and route the failure to a real message ('This version could not be saved — your version history is full'), which is also the missing trigger for offering a prune or an export.
chain: Versions -> NamedVersion -> autoCheckpoint -> unhandled rejection -> Recovery -> RUNTIME_FAULT_CAUGHT + crash sentinel -> the next load shows a recovery banner for a storage error

finding: Version storage is keyed by a projectId that starts as the literal 'default' and is only re-scoped asynchronously after the composer is ready, so anything captured before that resolves — and everything in the standalone editor, which never scopes at all — lands in one shared bucket.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:69 `private projectId: string = 'default'`; the constructor calls initialize() at :86 which loads under it. setProjectId is called from useComposerInit.ts:157 and useVersionSync.ts:41, both inside `if (siteId)` / `if (sid)` guards and both unawaited (`void`). VersionHistoryStorage.ts:66 `projectId: version.projectId || 'default'`.
fix: Construct the manager with the site id, or keep it dormant until one arrives — the comment at useComposerInit.ts:151-155 already describes exactly what a shared bucket does to a restore.

finding: The Command Palette's 'Clear history' emits the notification event instead of clearing anything — the undo stack is untouched, the state refresh recomputes the same values, and the command is a complete no-op with no feedback either way.
evidence: CommandPalette.tsx:155 `handler: () => { composer.emit(EVENTS.HISTORY_CLEARED, undefined); onClose(); }`. The real clear is HistoryManager.ts:746-761. useHistoryState.ts:59 subscribes to HISTORY_CLEARED and its updateState (:45-50) reads `composer.history.getHistoryStack()/canUndo()` — the unchanged stack. The sibling control in the same module does it correctly, with a two-step confirm: ActivityView.tsx:334-341 → useHistoryState.ts:81-86 → `composer.history.clear()`.
fix: Call `composer.history.clear()` and add the same two-step confirm ActivityView uses — if the command is ever wired, it is destructive and currently has no confirmation at all.

finding: While the All-changes list is mounted, its document-level keyboard handler swallows j, k, g, G, Enter, Space and Escape everywhere on the page — including inside canvas inline text editing, because the guard only exempts INPUT and TEXTAREA.
evidence: ActivityView.tsx:266-273 `if (document.activeElement?.tagName === 'INPUT' || ... === 'TEXTAREA') return;` then preventDefault on each key at :279-310. Canvas inline editing sets `el.contentEditable = 'true'` on the element's own tag (useCanvasInlineEdit.ts:116), so activeElement is an H1/P/DIV. The correct guard already exists in this codebase: useCanvasKeyboard.ts:70 `if ((e.target as HTMLElement)?.closest('input, textarea, [contenteditable]')) return;`.
fix: Adopt useCanvasKeyboard's guard verbatim, and scope the listener to the panel element rather than document.

finding: The History panel's stack goes stale after a project load or a version restore: recordCheckpoint emits nothing, so none of the four events the hook listens for fires, and the panel keeps rendering entries that no longer exist.
evidence: useHistoryState.ts:56-59 subscribes to HISTORY_RECORDED / UNDO / REDO / CLEARED only. HistoryManager.ts:353-358 recordCheckpoint pushes and emits nothing; :156-160 empties both stacks and calls recordCheckpoint('loaded') on PROJECT_LOADED. useComposerInit.ts:705-714 already learned this lesson for the Undo BUTTON and added PROJECT_LOADED + VERSION_RESTORED to its own list; useHistoryState never got the same treatment.
fix: Add EVENTS.PROJECT_LOADED and EVENTS.VERSION_RESTORED to useHistoryState's subscription list, matching useComposerInit.ts:705-714. Combined with MOD-G-16 this is what makes a stale row restore the wrong point.

finding: Nothing monitors storage quota anywhere, although the machinery for it is written: the reader has zero callers and both quota events are declared and never emitted — while four IndexedDB databases and several localStorage records grow without a ceiling.
evidence: StorageAdapter.ts:412-436 `getStorageQuota()` — a repo-wide grep returns only its own definition. EVENTS.STORAGE_QUOTA_WARNING / STORAGE_QUOTA_CRITICAL (events.ts:454-455) with payload types at :882-883, named nowhere. The only quota handling in the module is reactive and local: VersionHistoryStorage.ts:95-101 catches QuotaExceededError after the write has already failed.
fix: Poll getStorageQuota on an interval, emit the two events at their thresholds, and have the History panel offer 'export your versions' before the store is full rather than after a write has failed.
chain: Storage -> browser quota -> getStorageQuota (0 callers) -> STORAGE_QUOTA_WARNING / _CRITICAL (never emitted) -> Versions / Media / CMS -> the first symptom the user sees is a version that would not save

finding: Restoring a version silently reconfigures live third-party email services, because importProject runs the settings side effects. A version made before an API key was entered turns form notifications off with nothing said.
evidence: Composer.ts:568 importProject → applyProjectSettings; :723-748 `emailMarketingService.configure(emailConfig)` and `emailService.configure({...})` run off the snapshot's settings. Compounded by MOD-G-6: the redacted localStorage copy has no apiKey, so a project loaded from it and then versioned carries `apiKey: undefined` into every later restore.
fix: Name integrations in the restore confirm when the snapshot's integration settings differ from the current ones — a restore that changes who receives form submissions is not a visual change.
